method: Fixed central spotlight may fail. Peripheral-paper response compared with aligned SDR64 f/2.8 reference, exposure normalized using unclipped door areas. Gaussian sigma2 at quarter resolution suppresses individual-pixel noise and letter-edge alignment residuals. A 20% response deficit is an operational indicator of substantial highlight compression, not exact raw clipping. 10/15/25% thresholds and near-white-plateau area are retained for sensitivity checks. All raw temporal noise is measured independently without resizing/registration.
noise_normalization: Each static dark-door ROI is normalized to the same mean brightness. SDR4000 clips the bright wall at larger apertures, so that wall must not be used as the brightness reference here.
scope: All 49 original exposures retained, including samples with substantial peripheral clipping. The central mask is a subjective framing choice fixed across all images. Near-platform area means Y is at least 98.5% of the observed output ceiling (~3.295 SDR; ~26.36 NLOG), not proof every pixel is identically clipped. It is a practical highlight warning footprint. No absolute dynamic range is claimed.
